word:greek-nt:G0019.explanation: Agathōsynē means goodness, especially intrinsic goodness as a personal quality.

word:greek-nt:G0060.explanation: Agoraios refers to a lounger in the marketplace and may also suggest an agitator.

word:greek-nt:G0217.explanation: Halas means salt, a substance used for seasoning.

word:greek-nt:G0262.explanation: This word describes something that does not fade, lose its freshness, or pass away. It points to a quality of lasting beauty or value rather than something temporary and easily diminished. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Peter 5:4. Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, the word’s exact force in that passage depends on its context, but its central meaning is clear: enduring, unfading, and not subject to decay.

word:greek-nt:G0323.explanation: This word means “public appearance”—a revealing or presenting of someone before others. It describes the idea of becoming openly visible or being brought into public view, rather than remaining hidden or private. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Luke 1:80. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and sentence, but the central idea remains a public presentation or appearance.

word:greek-nt:G0451.explanation: Anna is a personal name rather than a word that describes an action, quality, or condition. It identifies one individual in the Greek New Testament, and its single occurrence is in Luke 2:36. Because the word is a name, its main function is to identify the person, not to express a general idea or instruction. The English rendering is also “Anna,” so there is no separate descriptive sense to add.

word:greek-nt:G0525.explanation: Apallassō means to release, set free, or be rid of someone or something.

word:greek-nt:G0590.explanation: Apodemos means away from home and staying in another country. It can describe someone going away on a journey, as in a man who leaves his house.

word:greek-nt:G0716.explanation: Harma means a chariot or vehicle.

word:greek-nt:G0837.explanation: Auxō means to increase or grow, describing something becoming greater.

word:greek-nt:G0842.explanation: Autarkēs means self-sufficient, contented, or satisfied.

word:greek-nt:G0914.explanation: Barachias is a personal name. In the passage, Barachias is identified as Zechariah’s father.

word:greek-nt:G0958.explanation: Beniamin is the personal name Benjamin.

word:greek-nt:G1045.explanation: Gad is one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

word:greek-nt:G1089.explanation: Geuomai means to taste; it can also mean to experience. It refers to tasting a drink and can describe experiencing death.

word:greek-nt:G1171.explanation: Deinōs means terribly, vehemently, or grievously.

word:greek-nt:G1193.explanation: Dermatinos means made of hide or leather.

word:greek-nt:G1203.explanation: Despotes means a lord or master, a title for someone with authority. It can describe human masters who have servants under them. It can also be used in addressing God, who is identified as the creator of heaven, earth, and sea.

word:greek-nt:G1412.explanation: Dynamoō means to strengthen or be strengthened.

word:greek-nt:G1539.explanation: Always means continually or on every occasion. It describes something that happens repeatedly or remains true without interruption, and it functions as an adverb, telling when or how consistently an action occurs. In the Greek New Testament, this word appears once, in 2 Peter 1:15. Its exact force in that verse is understood from the surrounding sentence, but its basic meaning is clear: the action or condition is presented as ongoing or consistently recurring.

word:greek-nt:G1621.explanation: Ektinassō means to shake off or shake out.

word:greek-nt:G1724.explanation: Enalios means marine or living in the sea.

word:greek-nt:G1786.explanation: This word means “resident,” referring to someone who lives in a particular place. It describes a local inhabitant rather than a visitor or temporary stranger. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Acts 21:12. The word itself identifies people by their connection with the place where they live; the precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and its actual wording.

word:greek-nt:G1863.explanation: Epago means to bring something upon someone, or to cause it to be counted against them. For example, it describes bringing a man’s blood upon people.

word:greek-nt:G1881.explanation: Epanistēmi means to rise up against or rebel against.

word:greek-nt:G1966.explanation: Epeimi refers to the next day.

word:greek-nt:G1988.explanation: Epistates means master, a title used when addressing Jesus.

word:greek-nt:G2097.explanation: Euangelizō means to bring good news or preach good tidings.

word:greek-nt:G2138.explanation: This Greek New Testament word describes someone who is compliant or submissive—ready to yield rather than resist. It functions as a description of a person’s disposition or response toward others. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in James 3:17. Its basic sense can therefore be stated simply: a person who is willing to comply or submit. The surrounding verse supplies the specific force of that description, but the word itself carries this clear idea.

word:greek-nt:G2174.explanation: This word means to be glad or to be cheerful. It describes an inwardly positive, joyful state rather than merely referring to an outward action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Philippians 2:19. Because the surrounding verse is not included here, the word’s precise force in that sentence cannot be described further. Its basic sense remains clear: it expresses gladness or cheerfulness, conveying a person’s positive emotional state.

word:greek-nt:G2211.explanation: Zenas is a personal name. In the passage, Zenas is identified as a lawyer.

word:greek-nt:G2365.explanation: Thugatrion means little daughter, or a young daughter.

word:greek-nt:G2435.explanation: Hilastērion means an atoning sacrifice, an offering made for sin. It can also refer to the covering of the ark.

word:greek-nt:G2480.explanation: Ischuō means to be strong or to have strength, and it can also mean to be able.

word:greek-nt:G2527.explanation: This word means “at all.” It is an adverb that adds emphasis to the extent or scope of what is being said, marking something in an absolute or unrestricted way. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 4:18. Its exact force in that verse is determined by the surrounding sentence, but its basic sense is to stress whether something applies in any degree or without exception.

word:greek-nt:G2552.explanation: This word means “suffering,” referring to the experience of undergoing pain, hardship, or distress. It is a noun that names suffering itself rather than describing a person or action. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in James 5:10. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the central idea remains the experience of suffering endured by someone. The word therefore points to hardship as a real condition that a person may face, especially in the course of faithful living.

word:greek-nt:G2633.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “condemnation,” referring to an adverse judgment against someone. It presents the idea of a person or group standing under a condemning verdict, rather than simply describing an accusation or criticism. The word occurs two times in the Greek New Testament, both in 2 Corinthians. Its precise force in either passage depends on the surrounding sentence and argument, but its central meaning remains the judgment of condemnation itself.

word:greek-nt:G2710.explanation: This word means “to make full use of” or “to use up.” It describes using something fully or taking the fullest benefit from it, rather than merely making limited use of it. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in 1 Corinthians. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central idea remains complete or fullest use. The word therefore points to using an opportunity, resource, or privilege to its full extent, according to the action being described.

word:greek-nt:G2769.explanation: Keration means a husk or pod of the carob.

word:greek-nt:G2831.explanation: This word describes being tossed back and forth by waves, or being thrown about like something unable to remain steady. It presents movement caused by waves rather than deliberate travel, so its central idea is wave-driven instability and motion. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Ephesians 4:14. The precise force in that verse depends on its surrounding wording, but the word itself points plainly to being tossed or shaken by wave-like movement.

word:greek-nt:G2992.explanation: Laos means a people. It can describe a distinct people associated with someone. More rarely, it refers to people generally.

word:greek-nt:G3007.explanation: Leipō means to lack or be wanting, describing something that is missing or insufficient.

word:greek-nt:G3072.explanation: This word means “in Lycaonian,” identifying the language being spoken rather than naming a person, place, or object. It functions as a language description, telling the reader that words were spoken in Lycaonian. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 14:11. The precise significance of the statement depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but the word itself points specifically to speech expressed in the Lycaonian language.

word:greek-nt:G3155.explanation: Maten means in vain, or to no purpose.

word:greek-nt:G3199.explanation: Melei means to care about something or be concerned with it.

word:greek-nt:G3326.explanation: Meta means with or after, depending on the context. It can mark people in company or a time that follows an earlier event.

word:greek-nt:G3384.explanation: Mētēr means mother. It names Mary as Jesus’ mother and appears in the instruction to honor one’s mother.

word:greek-nt:G3559.explanation: This word means an admonition or warning—a serious word of counsel intended to alert someone and guide them toward what is right. It names the act or message of caution, rather than merely describing a feeling or private thought. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs three times, in 1 Corinthians, Ephesians, and Titus. Its English rendering is consistently “admonition,” with “warning” also appearing once, showing that both counsel and alerting are part of its ordinary sense. The surrounding verse determines the specific situation in which the admonition is given.

word:greek-nt:G3595.explanation: This word means a guide or leader: a person who directs others and helps show them the way. It describes someone serving in a guiding role, whether that guidance is presented positively or exposed as unreliable. The word appears five times in the Greek New Testament, including passages in Matthew, Acts, and Romans. Its basic sense remains focused on a person who leads others rather than on the path, teaching, or destination itself.

word:greek-nt:G3634.explanation: Hoios means “of what kind,” expressed as “such as.”

word:greek-nt:G3678.explanation: This Greek New Testament word refers to a young donkey. It names the animal itself rather than describing an action, attitude, or spiritual quality. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at John 12:14. Its basic meaning is therefore specific and concrete: a donkey that is young. The surrounding passage is needed to explain how the animal functions in that verse, but the word’s lexical sense remains this straightforward designation.

word:greek-nt:G3696.explanation: Hoplon means an instrument; in the plural, it can mean weapons. It is used for instruments of righteousness and for weapons of warfare.

word:greek-nt:G3722.explanation: Orthros means early dawn or daybreak.

word:greek-nt:G3757.explanation: Οὗ means where, referring to a place.

word:greek-nt:G3829.explanation: This word means “inn,” referring to a lodging place where travelers could stay. It is a noun describing the destination or facility itself, rather than a person or an action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs only once, in Luke 10:34. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its ordinary meaning is a place providing accommodation for travelers.

word:greek-nt:G3850.explanation: Parabole means a comparison or parable. For example, a parable compares the Kingdom of Heaven to yeast hidden in meal.

word:greek-nt:G3973.explanation: Pauō means to cease or stop. It can also mean to cause something to cease.

word:greek-nt:G3991.explanation: Pemptos means fifth, identifying the fifth place in an ordered series. It marks the fifth seal, the fifth angel, and the fifth item in a list.

word:greek-nt:G4020.explanation: Periergazomai means to be a busybody.

word:greek-nt:G4095.explanation: Pino means to drink. Scripture uses it for the simple act of drinking wine and for drinking from a cup.

word:greek-nt:G4222.explanation: Potizō means to give someone a drink or to water something.

word:greek-nt:G4257.explanation: This word means to hear about something beforehand—to receive news or information before a later point. It describes prior knowledge gained through hearing, rather than seeing or discovering something personally. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Colossians 1:5. The precise force of the word in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea remains receiving information in advance.

word:greek-nt:G4334.explanation: Proserchomai means to come to, come near, or approach.

word:greek-nt:G4396.explanation: Prophetes means a prophet, a person gifted at explaining divine truth. A prophet is one through whom a message is spoken.

word:greek-nt:G4455.explanation: Pōpote means at any time, or ever.

word:greek-nt:G4499.explanation: The word means “Rhodes,” a proper name used to identify a place. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 21:1. Because the available wording gives the name but not the surrounding verse text, its safest lexical explanation is simply the place-name itself; the passage context supplies the specific role it has there within the narrative for readers.

word:greek-nt:G4507.explanation: Rhyparia means filth, pollution, or defilement.

word:greek-nt:G4572.explanation: Seautou means “of yourself” or “yourself.” It can describe showing yourself. It also appears in the instruction to love your neighbor as yourself.

word:greek-nt:G4626.explanation: Skaptō means to dig or excavate.

word:greek-nt:G4684.explanation: Spatalaō means to indulge in pleasure.

policy.futureRepairGate: Reopen only after a verified source-alignment, lexical-identity, or evidence-view correction materially changes the closed evidence.
policy.priorReviewerNotes: The lexical and Scripture evidence supports the verb meaning “establish/strengthen,” but the supplied identity is στιβάς/stibas while the displayed form and evidence correspond to στηρίξαι/στηρίζω. The explanation therefore assigns the supported verb meaning to the wrong lexical identity.

word:greek-nt:G4828.explanation: This word means “testifies with” or “to testify with”: it describes giving confirming testimony alongside another witness or truth. It expresses agreement in bearing witness, rather than merely speaking or making a claim. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs three times, all in Romans, and is rendered with the idea of testifying or testifying together. Its exact force in any sentence depends on what person or truth is being confirmed there. [p03:word:greek-nt:G4828:identity] [p03:word:greek-nt:G4828:occurrences]

word:greek-nt:G4864.explanation: Synagōgē means an assembly or congregation. It can also refer to the place where people gather.

word:greek-nt:G4961.explanation: Systratiōtēs means a fellow soldier in the Christian faith. It is applied to Epaphroditus and Archippus.

word:greek-nt:G4983.explanation: Sōma means body, referring to a person’s body or to bodies in the plural. It can also refer to a collective body, as when many are described as one body.

word:greek-nt:G5214.explanation: Hymneō means to sing hymns. It also describes praising God in song, as when Paul and Silas sang praises to God.

word:greek-nt:G5258.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “sleep,” referring to the condition of being asleep or resting. It appears six times in five New Testament verses, so it is a recurring everyday term rather than a rare or specialized expression. The word identifies sleep itself; the surrounding sentence determines how that basic idea functions in a particular passage. Its central meaning remains straightforward: sleep.

word:greek-nt:G5342.explanation: Pherō means to carry, bear, or bring. It can also describe leading someone away.

word:greek-nt:G5401.explanation: Phobos means fear, terror, or alarm.

word:greek-nt:G5508.explanation: Chios, also called Kios, is the name of an island or place. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, in Acts 20:15, and functions as a geographical name rather than a description of a person, action, or quality. The word itself identifies the location named in that passage; understanding its specific role there requires the surrounding verse and passage. Its meaning is therefore straightforward: Chios is a place-name referring to the island of Chios.

word:greek-nt:G5544.explanation: Chrestotes means goodness, kindness, or gentleness.
